decision: Is this copy clear, concrete and defensible enough to publish, and which claims still need proof?
limitations: It applies fixed word lists and readability rules to the text you paste. It cannot see how buyers respond, so a high score is not a conversion forecast.
It cannot tell whether the message is right. Copy can score well and still miss the positioning or break the brand voice; judge that yourself.
Concreteness counts numbers and names, not whether they are true. A made-up figure raises the score, so every number still needs proof on file.
Short copy gets an indicative score only (it wants about 25 words or more); a two-word input scored 100. Score a full section, not a headline on its own.
review: Whoever owns the page checks the draft against the positioning and the brand voice, and the founder confirms the proof behind every number and named customer before it ships.
